# Photon fine-density cost control

Source freeze: 2026-10-05. This is a **quality-changing cost control**, not an
accepted LOD optimization, filtered density approximation, isolated texture-fetch
budget or demonstrated performance gain. It tests whether fine 3D cumulus-density
sampling merits the later projected-detail work in
[PROJECTED_DETAIL_LOD_PLAN](PROJECTED_DETAIL_LOD_PLAN.md).

## Exact scope, baseline and activation

Original Photon v1.3b by Benjamin Stott (SixthSurge), version ID `gUv7fBPN`, local
`dev/upstream/photon_v1.3b.zip`, SHA-256
`120897768eaa8cb1f14a3e98f88dff009ae3204ee3b96904a4fe8586edfc1ead`.
The original LICENSE is preserved byte-for-byte, SHA-256
`514402d18eedb0afe374344ca9f0fe87b7399779518184b8fc64e31674555fc5`.
Retain [Photon attribution](../patches/photon/ATTRIBUTION.md); the mod's MIT
license does not replace the upstream shader terms.

Only two upstream payloads change:

| Member | Original SHA-256 | Private source change |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `shaders/include/sky/clouds/cumulus.glsl` | `1923542cd9ad862a6166a542dbdcb1597fd70316e4338b236deefc2ccb932ba5` | Gated two-field declarations and fine `worley_1` fetch site, original lines 81–82 |
| `shaders/settings.glsl` | `93401d268fe859cc1df81929ad41156757a98db80f80cf32af80d9cdca96c394` | Default-off private option |

`SHADERLOD_DENSITY_DETAIL_COST_CONTROL` defaults off. When it is on and the
program defines `PROGRAM_DEFERRED1`, strict bridge version 2/global enabled 1
uses a declared `worley_1=0.5` diagnostic. Absent/unknown bridge, invalid enable
value, global off, other programs or private off retains the literal original
fine texture sample. The branch encloses the fetch itself. Only existing
`shaderlodBridgeVersion` and `shaderlodEnabled` are consumed; no per-effect policy,
ratio, preset, near/far, transition or debug field is wired.

Overworld entry: `shaders/world0/deferred1.fsh` → `program/d1_clouds.fsh` →
`clouds.glsl` → `draw_cumulus_clouds`/`clouds_cumulus_density`.
The intervention affects that main pass's cumulus primary and secondary density
evaluations. Cached sky (`PROGRAM_DEFERRED0`), preparation/cloud shadows, other
cloud layers, water, materials, lighting and reconstruction remain source original.

Coarse `worley_0`, coverage and shell checks, original primary/light/ambient count
constants, march extent/step length, primary/secondary seeds, phase functions and
all upstream early-exit statements remain unchanged. However, replacing fine
erosion changes density, occupancy, accumulated transmittance and apparent
distance; those changes can alter actual early exits and executed secondary work.
It may substantially change cloud appearance. A faster result cannot establish a
quality-equivalent gain or assign an isolated cost to one texture instruction.

0.5 is a declared diagnostic, not a measured texture mean. Squaring and nonlinear
density contrast mean that even the actual raw texture mean would not preserve
mean opacity. No calibration or corrective coefficients are claimed. This control
has no distance/footprint threshold or quality transition. Upstream positions
remain atmosphere coordinates; any later LOD must convert actual observer/sample
distance to block units with `CLOUDS_SCALE`, as the separate plan specifies.

## Builder and static evidence

Owned new files are the builder, manifest, test module and this document. Builder
`scripts/build_photon_density_detail_probe.py` verifies archive/member/license
pins, reviewed unique anchors, disabled/enabled fingerprints and exact modification
scope. It accepts original/disabled/enabled arms, refuses output outside ignored
`build/` and cannot overwrite the original archive. All upstream payload names and
bytes outside the two members remain unchanged. One metadata member is added:
`shaderlod-density-detail-probe.json`.

Ran:

```sh
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_photon_density_detail_probe.py' -v
```

Eight source/scalar fixtures passed in 0.018 seconds. They verify default-off and
non-main-program byte parity for every original member, the sole fine-fetch source
intervention, strict activation, option/license/member scope, rejected source or
manifest mutations, literal original fallback, and a counterexample to nonlinear
mean/occupancy preservation. No output ZIP, GLSL compiler, game, image, physical
fetch-count or GPU timing check was performed by this worker.

After review, root/runtime operator can assemble once and freeze output hashes:

```sh
python3 scripts/build_photon_density_detail_probe.py --arm original
python3 scripts/build_photon_density_detail_probe.py --arm disabled
python3 scripts/build_photon_density_detail_probe.py --arm enabled
```

Default outputs are `build/Photon-DensityDetailCostControl-{arm}.zip`. Metadata
keys include `experiment=photon-cumulus-fine-density-cost-control`, `arm`,
`base_version/base_sha256`, `manifest_sha256`, `switch/switch_enabled`,
`modified_upstream_files`, `member_sha256`, `license_sha256`,
`unchanged_upstream_member_count`, `consumed_core_fields`, `activation`,
`program_scope`, `diagnostic_fine_noise=0.5`,
`quality_class=quality_changing_cost_control`, `source_policy`,
`physical_work_caveat`, `runtime_compilation=unverified` and `gpu_benefit=unmeasured`.
Use this explicit intervention class when qualifying profile/source differences;
do not silently classify it as ordinary upstream-quality parity.

## Runtime gate and stopping boundary

Root/runtime operator owns assembly, driver compilation, client focus, reloads,
captures and GPU measurements. First prove a main-pass cumulus-visible scene and
settled literal original OFF behavior. Then inspect the enabled cloud image before
timing; if clouds vanish or the signal depends on gross opacity changes, retain
that failed diagnostic and stop rather than treating it as an optimization.

Existing coastal scene source for a fresh immutable copy is
`run-workloads/photon-ssr-cost-controls-r1/coastalwater/high`, Overworld
x500.5/y68/z660.5, yaw87.38/pitch3.735, time12500/clear. Cloud visibility is not
established by shader options alone; check a matched rendered capture. Prior
original coastal measurement option hash is
`ecedfafc0a911b154db42ed786ffc468a694097ecacfb99852efeaa3dd6a5669`;
original forest hash is
`4efc7af7742bc445adf2b3b1454aa448a557e1d4b024103dd5b9f5758ed68745`.
Those are distinct profiles despite common cloud factor 4/counts 40/20/6/2.

Run a short original/default-off/enabled smoke, then repeated same-source global
OFF/ON frame-only intervals with matched resolution/preset/scene/weather, warmup,
quiet agent CPU activity and balanced order. Record total-frame and GPU median,
tail, variability and actual global values; keep instrumentation/readback outside
timed windows. Confirm no fallback and ordinary cloud visibility; a narrow
linked-field readback alone does not prove execution of the density path. If the
aggregate signal is flat/regressive, stop before calibration or projected-detail
implementation. If useful, require later full-near/edge preservation, controlled
far filtering, motion/weather/temporal quality and DH/noDH acceptance separately.

# Photon LUT runtime prerequisite R1

2026-10-07 10:56–11:03 PDT. One protected, untimed baseline launch proves the
current Performance deferred4 atmosphere LUT has the single-level sampling
contract required by the isolated sky-branch pilot. This proves bound runtime
state, not executed texture reads, patch equivalence or an FPS improvement.
The 11:16 harness reassessment and 11:26 first-screen boundary remain unchanged.

`/root/photon_lut_runtime_prerequisite` owned the client for this one run. Root
explicitly authorized two existing dev-only files: `SettledConsumerUniforms.java`
and `timing/CloudSamplerStateProbe.java`. Existing compiled-source/pass/Program/
pipeline hooks are reused; no mixin/controller/global sampler/history framework
was added. The new explicit `photon-atmosphere-lut` request accepts only the
pinned baseline archive and three member hashes, deferred4, and at least 3000 ms
of settlement after successful public Apply. It records both actual fragment
texts and calls the existing bounded sampler inventory at that joined quad HEAD.
Existing typed consumer modes and the guarded history getter retain their paths.
Ordinary absent-request behavior remains inactive. No relevant standalone test
seam exists for this GL/context hook; compilation and the actual run were checked.

The persisted [preprocessed fragment](../dev/logs/photon-sky-branch-r1/prerequisite/preprocessed_fragment.fsh)

declares `uniform sampler3D depthtex0; // atmosphere scattering LUT` and the
atmosphere lookup calls. The actual [transformed fragment](../dev/logs/photon-sky-branch-r1/prerequisite/transformed_fragment.fsh)
SHA256 `c377c32da1c70d94483df1e4c77dfa61d4a77c4449f73e9307d7db1418cc405a`
remaps that declaration and its lookup operands to `customtex0`.

| Actual customtex0 property | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Active type / size / location | sampler3D (35679) / 1 / 58 |
| Sampler unit / bound texture | 12 / 56 |
| Bound sampler object | 0; effective parameters come from texture |
| Level-zero dimensions / format | 32 × 64 × 32 / RGB16F (34843) |
| Texture base / max level | 0 / 0 |
| Effective min / mag filter | GL_LINEAR / GL_LINEAR |
| Effective min / max LOD / bias | 0 / 0 / 0 |

No GL error state was consumed. These getters do not inspect LUT contents,
other mip images, completeness, driver instruction counts or implicit derivative
behavior. They establish the actual single-level/filter contract for this draw
and pinned stack. The pilot's explicit level-zero lookups still need its own
rendered acceptance and quality checks.

# Photon fine-density cost-control runtime plan

2026-10-05 source-only checkpoint. Root owns client/GPU/build. This runtime
owner initially owned only this document; root subsequently authorized the
small shared-copy refactor and density wrapper/tests below. No real archive,
profile/save, config, client, compiler or timing changes were made by this owner
in this wave. The AO pilot
is terminal and is not repeated. Builder/manifest/test ownership belongs to
`lod_opportunities`; source freeze and root's fresh runtime handoff are required
before execution.

## Bounded question and reviewed source contract

Measure whether main-pass cumulus fine-density sampling is worth implementing
as projected procedural-detail LOD. The diagnostic replaces the fine
`worley_1` 3D texture value with declared 0.5. Coarse density, literal ray
counts/extents/seeds, other passes and cloud reconstruction remain original.
The replacement changes nonlinear density, occupancy, transmittance and early
exits. A faster result is a quality-changing source intervention, not an
isolated fetch budget, calibrated mean-opacity approximation, quality-equivalent
LOD gain or progress toward the accepted 50% throughput target. A flat or
regressive first result ends this candidate before calibration work.

The worker and runtime plan agree on:

| Item | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| Builder | `scripts/build_photon_density_detail_probe.py` |
| Source manifest | `patches/photon-experiments/density-detail-probe.json` |
| Original archive | Photon v1.3b, SHA-256 `120897768eaa8cb1f14a3e98f88dff009ae3204ee3b96904a4fe8586edfc1ead` |
| Private archive | `build/Photon-DensityDetailCostControl-disabled.zip` |
| Metadata member | `shaderlod-density-detail-probe.json` |
| Modified members | `shaders/include/sky/clouds/cumulus.glsl`, `shaders/settings.glsl` only |
| Private gate | `SHADERLOD_DENSITY_DETAIL_COST_CONTROL`, default off |
| Activation | gate AND PROGRAM_DEFERRED1 AND core version 2 AND global enabled exactly 1 |
| Diagnostic value | 0.5, `quality_changing_cost_control` |
| Core source consumption | version/global only under selected gate; no effect-extension consumer |
| Fallback | original fine fetch for gate off/other programs/unknown or absent core/global off |

Qualify the private archive against the worker's frozen manifest SHA-256 and
its recomputed `patch_members(..., 'disabled')`, then compare every upstream
member. Require exactly two changed files, the one metadata extra member,
unchanged original LICENSE and no missing/unsafe/duplicate/additional files.
Check base pin, manifest/member/license hashes, default-off gate and all frozen
metadata fields, including diagnostic/quality/program/activation/physical caveats.
Compute the resulting archive
SHA-256 after source qualification and preserve it throughout the run. Do not
accept an arbitrary archive path/hash list. For the rejected r1 attempt, the worker froze manifest SHA-256
`5b66b98cf065857d4df66e0ebbdcfbec281e619e8cde85e8dc58e44fc46fb1bd`,
patched cumulus member
`e64f2c71ce370203ab506f14e54ff64230013cf0f7eef5fe5e56e3ad2ae25db9`
and disabled settings member
`18914450d1be097f7fd2f1cb8c620ff2338200a4ea61a7902d140a3f8ec4b7ad`.
Root assembled the actual default-off archive at SHA-256
`0c0ac07a08a3c1e2c58658aabea95a564cc425795ff91c6a6b77bc0d8f2287d6`.
These are retained r1 source/assembly evidence, not current corrected gate or a
measured saving. The corrected source freeze is recorded below; a fresh corrected

## Minimal preparation reuse source freeze

The existing AO preparer already owns the useful invariant code: fresh/ignored
output validation, live-client rejection, all-source stopped-save locks,
canonical equal-world copies, source/provenance hash guards, fresh noDH removal,
source history preservation, per-arm config/pack setup and failure retention.
Its AO qualifier, private gate, fixed manifest path and GTAO requirements are
not valid density-control identities. Reusing it by monkeypatching module
globals would silently weaken pins and is rejected.

Root authorized and this owner implemented explicit parameters in the existing
copy orchestration for the read-only source inspector, experiment identity,
preparation marker name and qualification manifest key. Source manifest identity
comes from the qualified inspector record. Defaults preserve the AO contract.
The inspector returns the existing qualified scene record shape; the locked
copy loop remains one implementation and validates/fingerprints its source
record before and after copying. A density wrapper supplies a separately
pinned density archive/source inspector and cloud option requirements, then
delegates the cloning operation. This adds explicit arguments and a pinned
qualifier wrapper; no second copying framework,
universal patch registry, globals substitution or timing-harness edit.

New `scripts/prepare_photon_density_detail_profiles.py` reuses `archive_contents`, `archive_defaults`,
`filter_effective_options`, `normalize_requested_options`, scene/control and
runtime-lock validation primitives. Its dedicated source contract replaces the
AO-specific source test, not the common upstream option parity checks. Both
private arms write the same true density gate. Preserve the exact original
archive/mod-absent baseline and the complete actual member diff.

The unchanged AO test module passed all seven fixtures after the refactor.
Five new `tests/test_photon_density_detail_profiles.py` fixtures passed, covering
fresh ignored coastal plans, full actual upstream/member/metadata qualification
in a temporary source-fixture ZIP and read-only original coastal inspection,
rejected member/metadata contamination, exact cloud settings/gate parity,
viewport/scene rejection and canonical tiny stopped-save copies through the
shared callback with density-specific markers/manifest identity. Source fixtures
are deleted and no production archive or real-world preparation is performed by
these tests. No Java, runtime classes, timing harness or shared shader was changed.

## Fixed focus, quiet timing and planned runner command

Choose **visible, non-iconified and continuously unfocused** during capture for
all three arms. Arm and acknowledge a bounded focus watcher **before starting
the runner**, without creating its output directory. After each new client has
applied its camera and entered the 45-second warmup, it brings Codex to the foreground exactly once
using the native app activation capability (or `/usr/bin/open -a Codex` on this
recorded Mac). Do this early in warmup, never during capture. Leave the game
visible and do not touch game/UI focus again until its timed window ends.
The existing WindowStateTracker must observe only focused=false throughout
every capture, no unknown/focus changes, visible=true/non-iconified, identical
1488×836 logical/2976×1672 framebuffer and fixed pacing. If the operator cannot
establish that policy before capture, preserve and reject that attempt. Do not
repair a mismatched focus sample by relabeling the manifest or inferring that
pause-on-lost-focus=false makes focus irrelevant.

Root pauses all other worker test processes, builds, archive assembly, encoders,
image reads/processing and GPU jobs before the first timed launch. Source text
reads and brief logs/status/checkpoint updates may continue. The operator does
only the existing runner, warmup focus setup and minimal log/status monitoring
during this pilot. Actual focus comes from the report, not the activation
command's success. Capture-start/end timestamps and any external work are
retained. Configured pacing is not observed host scheduling/thermal equivalence.

## Terminal checks and decision boundary

After all timed windows exit, validate the existing UUID/request/options/control,
loaded mod/dependency, fixed wetness, CPU/GPU and fresh PNG contracts. Explicitly
check native/radius/pose/time/weather at both boundaries, quiet-work qualification,
the fixed focus/pacing policy, fully equal patched option maps and unchanged
upstream options relative to original. Re-qualify source/member/metadata and
record generated secondary effects config startup/defaults separately.
The existing WorkloadSession has no core/extension uniform readback or physical
fetch counter: option/global/bridge registration and source gating are intended
activation evidence, not an observed texture-call count or density-field proof.
Title-screen success alone is insufficient; require actual in-world rendering.

Inspect original/off/on final images only after timing stops. Check near/far
cloud occupancy, edge shape, brightness/transmittance, sun halo, reflected light,
shoreline/water-glint and any unexpected other-pass change. Intentional density
differences must be reported, never treated as tolerated production quality.
Static scalar/source checks and unchanged counters do not establish driver
arithmetic/opacity equivalence. One still cannot establish movement/wind/reset
or temporal quality. DH compatibility/terrain rendering is a separate future
check, not a noDH result.

Report total-frame mean/median/tails, GPU intervals, CPU wall/thread timings,

If all .75 cost were area-scalable, .70 could provide 14.80% more FPS than .75.

# Photon integration

ShaderLOD is an explicit integration with pinned Photon v1.3b. The NeoForge mod
supplies live settings through Iris; a reviewed patch manifest lowers actual
sample/ray budgets in shadow PCF, screen-space shadows, GTAO/SSAO, volumetric
fog, LPV fog, volumetric clouds, water wave normals/parallax, SSR, and POM. Installing DH uses Photon's
existing combined buffers and projection transforms, with the same distance
policy applied to coarse terrain rather than excluding it.

These are rendering experiments. Static compilation establishes source validity;
it does not establish GPU savings or acceptable visual quality. The runtime
coordinator records driver/render and timing evidence in the active goal. The
Apple development profile disables some Photon features to fit its sampler
limit; SSR/POM/LPV checks can be static even when the comparison does not run them.

## Build and select

```sh
python3 scripts/build_shaderpack.py
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -p test_shaderpack.py -v
```

The builder writes `run/shaderpacks/Photon-ShaderLOD.zip`; select it in Iris.
The **ShaderLOD** options screen exposes enabled, mod bridge, geometry distances,
transition width, preset, separate cloud distances, and tier colors. Default
geometry distances are 32/96 blocks, with eight-block transition bands. Cloud
entry distances use independent 512/4096-block thresholds by default.
`SHADERLOD_CLOUD_TRANSITION` defaults to a 256-block band and can be narrowed
independently of the geometry transition.
The fallback preset is Performance. `SHADERLOD_PRESERVE_LIGHTING` defaults on:
shadow PCF, screen-space shadows, GTAO and SSAO keep original budgets in all
presets. This protects tree depth/occlusion while cloud, fog, water and optional
material/reflection reductions remain available. `SHADERLOD_CACHED_SKY` is an opt-in global
lighting/reflection approximation and is disabled by default.

The archive comes from the exact Photon ZIP in `dev/runtime.lock.json`, reviewed
literal replacements in `patches/photon/v1.3b.json`, and the new helper in
`shaderpacks/photon/shaders/include/shaderlod/lod.glsl`. Source SHA-256 guards
and unique anchors fail closed. Overlays cannot replace upstream files. Builds
normalize paths, timestamps, order, and permissions and embed provenance in
`shaderlod-build.json`. This setup adds no universal GLSL rewriting mechanism.

Photon's license and untouched source files remain byte-identical. Photon has a
custom license with redistribution restrictions through monetized platforms;
retain its license with substantial copies and review before distribution.

## Work reduction

Near quality preserves each original budget. Disabled LOD always selects near
quality, including when the mod config is selected. Budgets are caps: no preset
raises common Photon work, and the disabled comparison uses the same source and
common settings. Fractional caps round up and obey an effect-specific minimum.

| Preset | Medium budget fraction | Far budget fraction | Far AO |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| Balanced (0) | 75% | 50% | Reduced |
| Performance (1) | 50% | 25% | Reduced |
| Aggressive (2) | 25% | 12.5% | Bypassed |

The AO column and shadow/AO rows below describe the **legacy policy with
`SHADERLOD_PRESERVE_LIGHTING=false`**. With the default flag on, original PCF,
SSRT, GTAO and SSAO counts remain unchanged, including Aggressive far AO. This
shader option is independent of the Java preset; no new uniform is required.

Some effects have explicit discrete policies as well as these fractions:

| Effect | Actual modified work | Performance example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Shadow PCF | Filtering loop and initial early-out count | Original adaptive/4 initial → 2 medium → 1 far |
| Screen-space shadows | Depth ray loop, geometric spacing normalized | 10 → 5 → 3 depth samples maximum |
| GTAO | Slice count and both horizon ray lengths/counts; correct averaging | Default 2 slices × 2 rays × 3 steps = 12 → 4 → 2 depth reads maximum |
| SSAO | Depth sample loop, angle distribution, averaging | Original → half → quarter (minimum 2) |
| Air/end/water fog | March count and whole-ray optical integration spacing | 25 → 13 → 7 steps (minimum 3) |
| LPV fog | March count and normalized geometric distribution | 24 → 12 → 6 steps (minimum 3) |
| Cumulus/altocumulus/congestus clouds | Primary density march and attached lighting/ambient rays | Horizon 40 primary → 20 → 10 (minimum 4); 6 lighting → 3 → 2, 2 ambient → 1 |
| Water surface | Wave noise/Gerstner octaves in all three finite-difference height samples; parallax march | 3 octaves → 2 → 1; 4 parallax steps → 2 → off |
| SSR | Rough ray count, intersection/refinement loops; far bypass of environment trace | 4 rough rays → 2 → 1; 16 intersection → 8 → 0; sky fallback remains |
| POM | Height traversal step size, shadow sample loop, far bypass | Original samples → half budget → off inside POM's own range |

These are source-level maximum operations, not hardware texture fetch counts or
measured pass time. Photon already early-outs in many places. Gains depend on
scene coverage, occupancy, divergence, cache behavior, driver compilation, and
features actually enabled. Shadow-map generation, TAA, bloom, sky atmosphere,
voxel updates, water caustic-map generation, and thin cloud layers remain upstream.
We do not claim complete LOD of every Photon effect.

When lighting preservation is disabled, GTAO retains the same radial and angular extent with fewer samples and normalizes
by actual slice count. Aggressive far AO returns neutral occlusion and the
surface normal before constructing or marching any horizon ray. Screen-space
shadows and LPV preserve geometric ray extent by recalculating the initial step.
Fog keeps the whole volume extent and scattering equations but integrates with
larger steps: foreground light shafts can change even when the endpoint is far.
Water fog is capped by upstream at 50 blocks, so it usually reaches only medium
quality; this is intentional.

Clouds use the camera-to-shell **entry** distance in atmosphere coordinates,
divided by `CLOUDS_SCALE` to recover world blocks. Clouds just overhead retain
full quality even when sky depth is 1. Primary sample spacing preserves the
whole volume, secondary geometric rays preserve their original summed extent,
and optical integration uses actual spacing. Primary/secondary caps apply to
the live cloud pass. By default the cached sky-map keeps original work.
`SHADERLOD_CACHED_SKY` optionally lowers its cloud primary and secondary budgets:
Balanced remains full, Performance uses the medium caps, and Aggressive uses far
caps (12.5% before effect minima). Disabled LOD remains full with the option on.
The cached pass already uses half the live primary budget upstream. Its cloud
samples originate at a fixed sea-level atmosphere position, so this is explicitly
a global lighting/reflection approximation rather than live camera-distance LOD.
It retains primary and secondary ray extent and integration normalization. Sky
atmosphere, sun/moon, aurora, and the cached lighting-color texels stay unchanged.
Inspect reflected clouds and ambient lighting if enabling it; no gain is promised.
Cloud shading's scattering iterations and density formulas remain upstream.

A source-verified cloud-detailed experiment uses near128/far1024/transition64
(the explicit Iris option ranges now include those values). With cloud altitude
1200 atmosphere units, scale10, sea level64 and camera altitude95, the overhead
shell entry is approximately89 world blocks. The64-block band around128 starts
at96, preserving full overhead quality, and reaches fully medium at160. The old
fixed256 band would start at0 and inadvertently reduce some overhead pixels.
Far transition spans992–1056. Inputs clamp width to the threshold gap and twice
the near distance, preventing overlap and negative starts; inverted thresholds
are sanitized. These are experiment settings, not a revised default or measured
performance claim. Entering the cloud volume gives entry distance0, so that
whole ray retains full quality under this policy. Inspect cloud silhouettes and
movement alongside timing.
These coarser samples can lose small cloud details and introduce TAA noise.

Water wave normals select quality from `distance(world_pos, cameraPosition)` in
both vanilla translucent shading and the common DH water composition helper.
Each finite-difference height evaluation samples only the actual octave count and
renormalizes the geometric amplitude sum. Reduced count removes high-frequency
wave detail while retaining the low-frequency normal and all three derivative
samples. Water parallax reduces its march and octave budgets in medium quality;
far quality returns the original coordinate without a height march. Shadow
caustic-map generation keeps its original wave budget. This introduces no new
texture bindings and should be inspected for moving highlights and transitions.

SSR far quality bypasses environment depth raymarching and still computes sky
fallback and Fresnel. Near/mid/far policies apply through the common specular
helper, including translucent callers. Rough reflections use actual ray count
in their average. Current Mac common options may disable these paths.

POM already ends at 32 blocks by default, so ordinary 32/96 geometry boundaries
would save nothing. Its own bands are 50% and 85% of `POM_DISTANCE`, with a
10%-of-range transition width. Far POM bypasses UV displacement and self-shadow;
medium uses larger depth steps and fewer self-shadow samples. POM requires a
compatible normal/height resource pack and is not demonstrated by default blocks.

## DH and transitions

The deferred shading and AO passes reconstruct `position_view` from Photon's
combined depth and **combined inverse projection**. DH fragments therefore use
real camera distance and can select the far policy. The distant screen-space
shadow routine retains Photon's projection/depth choice and reduces its actual
march; PCF savings alone would end at the shadow-map boundary. Fog selects
Photon's DH inverse projection for DH depth; its back-position conversion also
uses that selected projection. No new sampler bindings were added.

The `dh_terrain`, `dh_water`, and `dh_shadow` entrypoints are unchanged. Terrain
quality changes in shared downstream effects; DH water gets the shared fog
policy. ShaderLOD does not change DH chunk geometry, generation, or mesh detail.

Tier transitions choose one budget per pixel with interleaved noise and temporal
rotation where available; they do not evaluate both paths and blend their cost.
Noise work is avoided outside transition bands for the deferred/AO classifiers.
Debug colors show green/amber/red tiers on opaque terrain including DH, excluding
sky and hand. They do not visualize actual executed sample counts. Later fog,
transparency and post-processing can modify the tint. Tier flips can shimmer,
especially without TAA; inspect movement as well as static images.

## Uniform contract

`SHADERLOD_USE_MOD_CONFIG` defaults on. Registered uniforms use sentinel 2 for
the expanded contract. Sentinel 1 remains accepted for earlier settings, with
preset falling back to the pack option. Missing/unregistered uniforms are zero,
so an absent mod uses all pack defaults. Disable mod config to test fallback.

| Uniform | GLSL type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `shaderlodBridgeVersion` | `int` | 2 selects expanded contract; 1 accepts original values |
| `shaderlodEnabled` | `int` | Nonzero enables reductions |
| `shaderlodNear` | `float` | Geometry near boundary in blocks |
| `shaderlodFar` | `float` | Geometry far boundary in blocks |
| `shaderlodTransition` | `float` | Entire geometry transition band width |
| `shaderlodDebug` | `int` | Nonzero enables tier colors |
| `shaderlodPreset` | `int` | 0 Balanced / 1 Performance / 2 Aggressive |

Cloud thresholds and relative material bands are shader policies; the cloud
thresholds have pack options, and are not new Java bridge uniforms. Configuring
geometry ranges does not reclassify all sky pixels as far. Iris uniform
registration is an internal hook bounded to the audited Iris version. Expression
custom uniforms in shader properties are a different mechanism; none are added
for Java-supplied names.

Packaging checks cover deterministic output, corrupted base/source rejection,
ambiguous/missing anchors, license retention, and byte preservation outside the
explicit manifest targets. With `glslangValidator`, the suite compiles deferred
shading, translucent shading, AO, clouds, cached sky, fog, terrain, DH terrain,
DH water, water composition, and shadow caustic generation across all dimensions and option variants including optional cached-sky LOD, bridge fallback,
disabled LOD, every preset, DH, SSAO/no AO, shadows toggles, and SSR/POM materials.
660 fragment compilation variants passed locally (11 programs × 3 dimensions × 20 option variants),
including the default preserved-lighting path, all three legacy lighting presets,
and legal close/inverted cloud option cases. Eight test methods also check that
candidate values exist in Iris's declared ranges and execute the actual cloud

Tests expand actual shader includes and join preprocessor continuations. This is

A two-client shared-GPU view is a visual comparison and cannot isolate speedup.

## Historical lighting reductions

The early PCF-only test and 2026-10-03 multi-effect GPU results used the legacy
lighting policy, before `SHADERLOD_PRESERVE_LIGHTING` existed. Reproducing those
budgets now requires explicitly disabling the preservation flag. The user
rejected lost distant tree depth/shadows for the small forest-scene saving;
preservation therefore defaults on. This flag preserves the four shadow/AO
operations named above, not every possible illumination effect. Opt-in cached
sky reduction remains a separate global lighting/reflection approximation and
should be evaluated independently.

## Initial comparison audit (2026-10-03)

The floating preview clients use the identical patched pack with LOD enabled
and disabled; ShaderLOD is loaded in both. This isolates the shader enable
switch, but is not a mod-absent baseline. Both share the Mac GPU and the reduced
option set. Recorded snapshots were ON 113/115 FPS and OFF 115/113 FPS; the
user also observed approximately equal FPS, sometimes ON 2–3% lower. These
observations do not establish a speedup or an isolated regression.

The patch does change the actual `shadow_pcf` sampling loops. However, Photon
already exits after its initial four lookups on uniformly lit or shadowed pixels:

| Shadow-map PCF region | Full/disabled | Medium | Far |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Uniformly lit or shadowed | 4 | 4 | 1 |
| Mixed edge, ordinary stone under current options | 7–11 | 4 | 1 |
| Large SSS blur | Up to 12 | 4 | 1 |
| Outside the shadow-map range | 0 | 0 | 0 |

These are GLSL sampler lookups, not raw hardware texel comparisons. With
variable penumbras disabled, ordinary full budgets follow
`min(12, int(6 + max(1, 0.125 / D²)))`, where the in-map shadow distortion
factor `D` is at least 0.15. The unchanged shadow distance is 128 blocks.
Far LOD becomes fully active at 100 blocks after its transition, leaving roughly
100–128 blocks of potential far savings; projection bounds can reduce that
range. Beyond it, Photon skips PCF and its screen-space shadow path is unchanged.

The sparse pillar fixture contains extensive sky, near floor, and uniformly
lit stone. It was suitable for visualizing zones, not a strong performance
kill test. Medium LOD often removes no lookups there. Clouds, GTAO, volumetric
fog, shadow-map generation, and translucent shading keep their upstream work.
Enabled LOD adds tier/noise calculations; their compiled cost and GPU branch
behavior have not been measured, and could outweigh small savings.

The next decisive check should visualize actual executed PCF lookup counts,
including zero for bypasses, and force far quality on shadow-mapped terrain.
Then time one client with alternating enabled/disabled states after warmup.
A temporary 32-sample versus one-sample stress mode can test the upper bound,
but must be reported as an artificial diagnostic rather than a normal-preset gain.

# Photon integration

ShaderLOD is an explicit integration with pinned Photon v1.3b. The NeoForge mod
supplies live settings through Iris; a reviewed patch manifest lowers actual
sample/ray budgets in shadow PCF, screen-space shadows, GTAO/SSAO, volumetric
fog, LPV fog, volumetric clouds, water wave normals/parallax, SSR, and POM. Installing DH uses Photon's
existing combined buffers and projection transforms, with the same distance
policy applied to coarse terrain rather than excluding it.

These are rendering experiments. Static compilation establishes source validity;
it does not establish GPU savings or acceptable visual quality. The runtime
coordinator records driver/render and timing evidence in the active goal. The
Apple development profile disables some Photon features to fit its sampler
limit; SSR/POM/LPV checks can be static even when the comparison does not run them.

## Build and select

```sh
python3 scripts/build_shaderpack.py
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -p test_shaderpack.py -v
```

The builder writes `run/shaderpacks/Photon-ShaderLOD.zip`; select it in Iris.
The **ShaderLOD** options screen exposes enabled, mod bridge, geometry distances,
transition width, preset, separate cloud distances, and tier colors. Default
geometry distances are 32/96 blocks, with eight-block transition bands. Cloud
entry distances use independent 512/4096-block thresholds with a 256-block band.
The fallback preset is Performance. `SHADERLOD_CACHED_SKY` is an opt-in global
lighting/reflection approximation and is disabled by default.

The archive comes from the exact Photon ZIP in `dev/runtime.lock.json`, reviewed
literal replacements in `patches/photon/v1.3b.json`, and the new helper in
`shaderpacks/photon/shaders/include/shaderlod/lod.glsl`. Source SHA-256 guards
and unique anchors fail closed. Overlays cannot replace upstream files. Builds
normalize paths, timestamps, order, and permissions and embed provenance in
`shaderlod-build.json`. This setup adds no universal GLSL rewriting mechanism.

Photon's license and untouched source files remain byte-identical. Photon has a
custom license with redistribution restrictions through monetized platforms;
retain its license with substantial copies and review before distribution.

## Work reduction

Near quality preserves each original budget. Disabled LOD always selects near
quality, including when the mod config is selected. Budgets are caps: no preset
raises common Photon work, and the disabled comparison uses the same source and
common settings. Fractional caps round up and obey an effect-specific minimum.

| Preset | Medium budget fraction | Far budget fraction | Far AO |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| Balanced (0) | 75% | 50% | Reduced |
| Performance (1) | 50% | 25% | Reduced |
| Aggressive (2) | 25% | 12.5% | Bypassed |

Some effects have explicit discrete policies as well as these fractions:

| Effect | Actual modified work | Performance example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Shadow PCF | Filtering loop and initial early-out count | Original adaptive/4 initial → 2 medium → 1 far |
| Screen-space shadows | Depth ray loop, geometric spacing normalized | 10 → 5 → 3 depth samples maximum |
| GTAO | Slice count and both horizon ray lengths/counts; correct averaging | Default 2 slices × 2 rays × 3 steps = 12 → 4 → 2 depth reads maximum |
| SSAO | Depth sample loop, angle distribution, averaging | Original → half → quarter (minimum 2) |
| Air/end/water fog | March count and whole-ray optical integration spacing | 25 → 13 → 7 steps (minimum 3) |
| LPV fog | March count and normalized geometric distribution | 24 → 12 → 6 steps (minimum 3) |
| Cumulus/altocumulus/congestus clouds | Primary density march and attached lighting/ambient rays | Horizon 40 primary → 20 → 10 (minimum 4); 6 lighting → 3 → 2, 2 ambient → 1 |
| Water surface | Wave noise/Gerstner octaves in all three finite-difference height samples; parallax march | 3 octaves → 2 → 1; 4 parallax steps → 2 → off |
| SSR | Rough ray count, intersection/refinement loops; far bypass of environment trace | 4 rough rays → 2 → 1; 16 intersection → 8 → 0; sky fallback remains |
| POM | Height traversal step size, shadow sample loop, far bypass | Original samples → half budget → off inside POM's own range |

These are source-level maximum operations, not hardware texture fetch counts or
measured pass time. Photon already early-outs in many places. Gains depend on
scene coverage, occupancy, divergence, cache behavior, driver compilation, and
features actually enabled. Shadow-map generation, TAA, bloom, sky atmosphere,
voxel updates, water caustic-map generation, and thin cloud layers remain upstream.
We do not claim complete LOD of every Photon effect.

GTAO retains the same radial and angular extent with fewer samples and normalizes
by actual slice count. Aggressive far AO returns neutral occlusion and the
surface normal before constructing or marching any horizon ray. Screen-space
shadows and LPV preserve geometric ray extent by recalculating the initial step.
Fog keeps the whole volume extent and scattering equations but integrates with
larger steps: foreground light shafts can change even when the endpoint is far.
Water fog is capped by upstream at 50 blocks, so it usually reaches only medium
quality; this is intentional.

Clouds use the camera-to-shell **entry** distance in atmosphere coordinates,
divided by `CLOUDS_SCALE` to recover world blocks. Clouds just overhead retain
full quality even when sky depth is 1. Primary sample spacing preserves the
whole volume, secondary geometric rays preserve their original summed extent,
and optical integration uses actual spacing. Primary/secondary caps apply to
the live cloud pass. By default the cached sky-map keeps original work.
`SHADERLOD_CACHED_SKY` optionally lowers its cloud primary and secondary budgets:
Balanced remains full, Performance uses the medium caps, and Aggressive uses far
caps (12.5% before effect minima). Disabled LOD remains full with the option on.
The cached pass already uses half the live primary budget upstream. Its cloud
samples originate at a fixed sea-level atmosphere position, so this is explicitly
a global lighting/reflection approximation rather than live camera-distance LOD.
It retains primary and secondary ray extent and integration normalization. Sky
atmosphere, sun/moon, aurora, and the cached lighting-color texels stay unchanged.
Inspect reflected clouds and ambient lighting if enabling it; no gain is promised.
Cloud shading's scattering iterations and density formulas remain upstream.
These coarser samples can lose small cloud details and introduce TAA noise.

Water wave normals select quality from `distance(world_pos, cameraPosition)` in
both vanilla translucent shading and the common DH water composition helper.
Each finite-difference height evaluation samples only the actual octave count and
renormalizes the geometric amplitude sum. Reduced count removes high-frequency
wave detail while retaining the low-frequency normal and all three derivative
samples. Water parallax reduces its march and octave budgets in medium quality;
far quality returns the original coordinate without a height march. Shadow
caustic-map generation keeps its original wave budget. This introduces no new
texture bindings and should be inspected for moving highlights and transitions.

SSR far quality bypasses environment depth raymarching and still computes sky
fallback and Fresnel. Near/mid/far policies apply through the common specular
helper, including translucent callers. Rough reflections use actual ray count
in their average. Current Mac common options may disable these paths.

POM already ends at 32 blocks by default, so ordinary 32/96 geometry boundaries
would save nothing. Its own bands are 50% and 85% of `POM_DISTANCE`, with a
10%-of-range transition width. Far POM bypasses UV displacement and self-shadow;
medium uses larger depth steps and fewer self-shadow samples. POM requires a
compatible normal/height resource pack and is not demonstrated by default blocks.

## DH and transitions

The deferred shading and AO passes reconstruct `position_view` from Photon's
combined depth and **combined inverse projection**. DH fragments therefore use
real camera distance and can select the far policy. The distant screen-space
shadow routine retains Photon's projection/depth choice and reduces its actual
march; PCF savings alone would end at the shadow-map boundary. Fog selects
Photon's DH inverse projection for DH depth; its back-position conversion also
uses that selected projection. No new sampler bindings were added.

The `dh_terrain`, `dh_water`, and `dh_shadow` entrypoints are unchanged. Terrain
quality changes in shared downstream effects; DH water gets the shared fog
policy. ShaderLOD does not change DH chunk geometry, generation, or mesh detail.

Tier transitions choose one budget per pixel with interleaved noise and temporal
rotation where available; they do not evaluate both paths and blend their cost.
Noise work is avoided outside transition bands for the deferred/AO classifiers.
Debug colors show green/amber/red tiers on opaque terrain including DH, excluding
sky and hand. They do not visualize actual executed sample counts. Later fog,
transparency and post-processing can modify the tint. Tier flips can shimmer,
especially without TAA; inspect movement as well as static images.

## Uniform contract

`SHADERLOD_USE_MOD_CONFIG` defaults on. Registered uniforms use sentinel 2 for
the expanded contract. Sentinel 1 remains accepted for earlier settings, with
preset falling back to the pack option. Missing/unregistered uniforms are zero,
so an absent mod uses all pack defaults. Disable mod config to test fallback.

| Uniform | GLSL type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `shaderlodBridgeVersion` | `int` | 2 selects expanded contract; 1 accepts original values |
| `shaderlodEnabled` | `int` | Nonzero enables reductions |
| `shaderlodNear` | `float` | Geometry near boundary in blocks |
| `shaderlodFar` | `float` | Geometry far boundary in blocks |
| `shaderlodTransition` | `float` | Entire geometry transition band width |
| `shaderlodDebug` | `int` | Nonzero enables tier colors |
| `shaderlodPreset` | `int` | 0 Balanced / 1 Performance / 2 Aggressive |

Cloud thresholds and relative material bands are shader policies; the cloud
thresholds have pack options, and are not new Java bridge uniforms. Configuring
geometry ranges does not reclassify all sky pixels as far. Iris uniform
registration is an internal hook bounded to the audited Iris version. Expression
custom uniforms in shader properties are a different mechanism; none are added
for Java-supplied names.

## Verification

Packaging checks cover deterministic output, corrupted base/source rejection,
ambiguous/missing anchors, license retention, and byte preservation outside the
explicit manifest targets. With `glslangValidator`, the suite compiles deferred
shading, translucent shading, AO, clouds, cached sky, fog, terrain, DH terrain,
DH water, water composition, and shadow caustic generation across all dimensions and option variants including optional cached-sky LOD, bridge fallback,
disabled LOD, every preset, DH, SSAO/no AO, shadows toggles, and SSR/POM materials.
495 fragment compilation variants passed locally (11 programs × 3 dimensions × 15 option variants).
Tests expand actual shader includes and join preprocessor continuations. This is
GLSL syntax/type evidence, not Iris transformation or Apple GPU-driver evidence.

For runtime acceptance, keep common options and camera/scene identical, warm DH
terrain and temporal histories, inspect near/mid/far geometry and cloud details,
and use serial alternating LOD-on/off measurements with actual GPU queries.
A two-client shared-GPU view is a visual comparison and cannot isolate speedup.

## Initial comparison audit (2026-10-03)

The floating preview clients use the identical patched pack with LOD enabled
and disabled; ShaderLOD is loaded in both. This isolates the shader enable
switch, but is not a mod-absent baseline. Both share the Mac GPU and the reduced
option set. Recorded snapshots were ON 113/115 FPS and OFF 115/113 FPS; the
user also observed approximately equal FPS, sometimes ON 2–3% lower. These
observations do not establish a speedup or an isolated regression.

The patch does change the actual `shadow_pcf` sampling loops. However, Photon
already exits after its initial four lookups on uniformly lit or shadowed pixels:

| Shadow-map PCF region | Full/disabled | Medium | Far |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Uniformly lit or shadowed | 4 | 4 | 1 |
| Mixed edge, ordinary stone under current options | 7–11 | 4 | 1 |
| Large SSS blur | Up to 12 | 4 | 1 |
| Outside the shadow-map range | 0 | 0 | 0 |

These are GLSL sampler lookups, not raw hardware texel comparisons. With
variable penumbras disabled, ordinary full budgets follow
`min(12, int(6 + max(1, 0.125 / D²)))`, where the in-map shadow distortion
factor `D` is at least 0.15. The unchanged shadow distance is 128 blocks.
Far LOD becomes fully active at 100 blocks after its transition, leaving roughly
100–128 blocks of potential far savings; projection bounds can reduce that
range. Beyond it, Photon skips PCF and its screen-space shadow path is unchanged.

The sparse pillar fixture contains extensive sky, near floor, and uniformly
lit stone. It was suitable for visualizing zones, not a strong performance
kill test. Medium LOD often removes no lookups there. Clouds, GTAO, volumetric
fog, shadow-map generation, and translucent shading keep their upstream work.
Enabled LOD adds tier/noise calculations; their compiled cost and GPU branch
behavior have not been measured, and could outweigh small savings.

The next decisive check should visualize actual executed PCF lookup counts,
including zero for bypasses, and force far quality on shadow-mapped terrain.

## Why broad opaque rejection fails

- A back-facing ordinary opaque receiver is already skipped. SSS receivers enter
  intentionally: hardcoded plants have SSS 0.5 and leaves SSS 1. The active
  non-VPS `sss_approx` and its sheen remain shadow dependent even when NoL is
  negative. Rejecting those receivers loses foliage transmission/lighting.
- `diffuse_lighting.glsl:167` adds `B * (1 - shadows)`, where B includes AO,
  fourth-power skylight and BOUNCED_LIGHT_I. Zero diffuse orientation alone does
  not eliminate this dependency. Low or zero skylight does not eliminate the
  separate near-shadow direct-diffuse term on positive-facing surfaces.
- Opaque zero albedo is insufficient: ordinary dielectric f0 is 0.02 and the
  separate specular highlight is multiplied by shadows. Metals retain 0.5 of
  diffuse lighting intentionally; they are not purely specular receivers.
- Clouds cannot supply an active zero multiplier: CLOUD_SHADOWS is false here,
  giving exactly 1. Even enabled intensity 0.80 retains a 0.20 floor for
  nonnegative sampled transmission. Black light color is a valid finite-output
  whole-light zero case, but ordinary sunset/moonlight is not generally black:
  new-moon brightness is 0.5, not zero. There is no measured current-scene zero
  light-color coverage. POM's later zero visibility could avoid filtering in
  another configuration, but POM is inactive here.

These are source counterexamples and active-option exclusions, not image or
performance observations. Do not revive the rejected projected-footprint PCF
sample reduction from `PHOTON_SHADOW_BUDGET_REVIEW.md`.

## Exact water bound and minimal private patch shape

For finite valid original inputs, restrict to Overworld PROGRAM_GBUFFERS_WATER,
`is_water`, private option ON, a known enabled core bridge, SHADOW active and
**SHADOW_VPS absent**. Then the sufficient skip condition is:

```glsl
max_of(material.albedo) < eps && NoL <= eps
```

This uses precisely the existing output conditions and eps = 1e-6; it introduces
no brighter/darker threshold:

1. `diffuse_lighting.glsl:140–144` already returns vec3(0) for that albedo bound
   in PROGRAM_GBUFFERS_WATER, before consuming shadows or distance fade.
2. `specular_lighting.glsl:109–111` returns vec3(0) for that NoL bound. The
   highlight is the only remaining filtered-visibility consumer in this stage.
3. `pcss.glsl:223` initializes sss_depth to zero. Its only subsequent assignment
   in `get_filtered_shadows` is inside SHADOW_VPS. Thus active water absorption
   continues to receive precisely the original zero depth.
4. `water_absorption_approx` → `simple_fog.glsl:194–235` consumes unfiltered
   light_color/cloud_shadows, ambient light and sss_depth; it does not consume
   filtered visibility. Preserve that call and all absorption/scattering.
5. Keep `get_specular_reflections` unchanged. Water reflections and their
   analytic reflected fog do not use this receiver's filtered shadows.

Initialize shadows, sss_depth and shadow_distance_fade as today, and enclose only
this stage's original `get_filtered_shadows` call in the conditional. On eligible
skip, sss_depth stays 0; distance_fade is unconsumed because diffuse returned 0.
Retain every other stage/source path and private-OFF token parity. Unknown bridge,
unknown stage or VPS enabled must execute the original call. Explicitly exclude
invalid/nonfinite values rather than relying on ambiguous NaN max behavior.
No capability/effect consumption is claimed by this recommendation.

Coverage is physically plausible with current settings:
`get_water_material` multiplies underground texture highlight by
`1 - cube(linear_step(0, 0.5, skylight))`, exactly zero for skylight ≥ 0.5.
The separate edge highlight is zero where
`layer_dist * max(abs(direction_world.y), eps) >= 0.5`. Open water sufficiently
away from a shallow edge can therefore have zero albedo. Backlit wave facets can
have NoL ≤ eps even with an upward flat normal and a sun above the horizon.
These are possible source inputs, not an observed coastal pixel frequency.
Shore highlights and any water with positive albedo remain protected.

VPS is a hard boundary: its blocker search exports nonzero sss_depth, which water
absorption uses independently of the zero surface-lighting bound. Extending this
skip into VPS without retaining its depth computation changes underwater/direct
scattering. Non-water glass/foliage and all opaque stages remain outside this
first proposal.

## Work ceiling and next decisive experiment

An eligible in-domain receiver currently costs one noisetex fetch, bias/edge/
shadow-space calculations and **4 comparison lookups on uniform first-four
exits, up to 12 on mixed edges**. The PCF count is
`min(int(6 + filter_scale), 12)` with filter_scale ≥ 1; the existing first-four
all-lit/all-shadow exit is retained in the control. Out-of-domain receivers
already return before the noise/PCF work and must not inflate savings estimates.
VPS/color are disabled, so there is no avoided blocker march or colored fetch.
Opaque/deferred SSRT and shadow-map generation remain unchanged. A 50% eligible
water fraction would only halve this water receiver-filter work before divergence
and gate overhead; it does not imply 50% total-frame improvement. No stage-time
or total-frame millisecond ceiling has been measured.

Practical next experiment for root: a query-free private diagnostic that counts
water fragments, finite eligible fragments, original in-domain calls, actual PCF
comparison iterations and skipped calls/iterations. Record coherent small-region
coverage too; isolated eligible lanes may leave other lanes doing original work.

## Accepted source reasoning

The private helper
`shaderpacks/photon-contribution-tail/shaders/include/shaderlod/contribution_tail.glsl`
has the correct order-4 state at lines 118–128: amplitude, extinction, g and powder
are advanced after order 3, before its proposed early break and before evaluating
the next phase. The clone is byte-identical to the original scattering body after
removing only that injected decision. Original density, optical-depth marcher and
draw bodies are unchanged. Thus the prototype does not reduce primary/direct/sky
marches, alter optical normalization or delete surface lighting/shadow cues.

At lines 49–54, the finite sum calculates A4..A7 with the actual recurrence.
Photon's powder is not bounded by one: for finite nonnegative density its initial
range is [0,π), then the cosine mix stays between that value and one. Subsequent
`(p+sqrt(p))/2` stays positive and moves toward one. The helper's derived-state
powder ≤4 check conservatively covers this domain; no invalid geometric ratio
assumption is present. Falloff is in [0,.55], but `falloff*powder` can exceed one.

For every HG lobe, the maximum over angle is
`iso*(1+abs(g))/(1-abs(g))²`. Its value increases with abs(g). All original g
components are nonnegative and shrink by .8; at order 4 the largest possible g
is `.9*.8^4 = .36864`, below the helper's .5 guard. The weighted order-4 peak
therefore bounds all remaining positive/negative lobes, including the negative
third lobe. Lines 57–59 implement that bound correctly.

The remaining extinction sequence is E4, .4E4, .16E4, .064E4. With nonnegative
depths its largest attenuation is the order-7 value. Lines 62–67 use this same
upper attenuation for all four terms and form the correct direct-plus-ground-
plus-sky X and ambient Y envelopes. Shadow is guarded in [0,1], so both
`1-.5*shadow` and `.5*shadow` remain nonnegative; negative bounce retains original
work. Both components must fit the bound. Ambient/indirect scattering used for
lightning is not ignored.

The exact criterion is stricter than 2% omitted/prefix:
`bound/prefix <= .02*.99/1.01 ≈ .01960396`. For positive cells, the common
nonnegative scattering integral and primary transmittance preserve the component
bound through ray accumulation. This is a pre-color, pre-tonemap scalar guarantee
in exact arithmetic. Signed/extrapolated color transformations, exposure, HDR
cancellation, history/filtering and displayed-image error are outside that proof.

Wrapper lines 141–147 route core version other than exactly 2, global other than
exactly 1 and invalid inputs into the retained original function before clone or
bound work. Missing uniform zero behavior is a runtime assumption, not a linked
observation. The helper explicitly rejects nonfinite, negative and overly large
inputs, invalid cosine/shadow/blend, tiny extinction and invalid derived prefixes
or bounds. Rejected derived states finish all eight original orders in the clone.
Unknown controls retain original numerical work, while still paying the wrapper
branch; this is not an archive-byte or driver-timing parity claim.

## Expense and realistic saving ceiling

Every eligible occupied cell cuts orders 8→4. Its maximum logical cut is half
the order work, with all density/primary/secondary texture work retained.
The bound runs at the single decision for every valid occupied cell, including
those that do not skip: three exp components, three powder square roots, three
HG-peak divisions, finite guards, vector ALU and a potentially divergent break.
High order eligibility is therefore necessary, not sufficient, for a win.

Original cumulus contains four scalar exp sites per order, but its sky expression
is duplicated in X and Y. Assuming ordinary common-subexpression elimination,
there are three unique exp arguments per order: 24 original, 12 retained plus
three bound arguments =15 for an eligible cell; an ineligible cell can require
27. For a cost-unweighted eligible fraction q, this simple exp-site model changes
24 to `27-12q` per cell. It breaks even only when q>25%, and even q=1 saves at
most 37.5% of those unique exp evaluations. Without sharing, raw sites change
32 to `35-16q`, breaking even above 18.75%. Neither model counts driver issues,
latency, vectorization, branch coherence or wall/GPU time.

Four useful three-HG phase updates are skipped, saving up to 12 HG evaluations;
the final original phase update is unused and may already be removed. The finite
amplitude bound still performs the three powder updates needed for A5..A7, so
there is no guaranteed saving of those useful powder square roots. Ineligible
cells perform that recurrence in the bound and again when completing the series.
Texture fetch counts, primary transmittance and distant surface shadows do not
change. Duplicated retained/clone functions may also change registers, code size,
loop unrolling or scheduling; source equivalence does not measure that overhead.

If h is the original total-render cost fraction in this series and q its qualifying
cost fraction, ideal zero-overhead half-order removal saves at most `.5qh` of
elapsed time. A 20% FPS increase requires one-sixth less time, hence `qh>=1/3`
even before bound/fallback overhead. No ordinary h or q has been measured, and
synthetic grid eligibility must not be substituted. Instrumented pass timing is
not an ordinary frame budget; retain its prior instrumentation qualifications.

# Photon cloud history scale remapping design

2026-10-06. Bounded source design completed after pausing for root's quiet forest
timing bracket. No implementation, build, test suite, client or GPU operation
performed. No owned live processes. Root owns the client/GPU and integration.
Cloud remapping is a concrete candidate; native TAA preservation is a separate
falsification candidate. Neither has runtime quality or speed acceptance.

Pinned source: Photon v1.3b original SHA-256
120897768eaa8cb1f14a3e98f88dff009ae3204ee3b96904a4fe8586edfc1ead;
private R2 archive build/live-pixel-history-r2-enabled.zip SHA-256

## Result and assumptions

A previous-scale design is feasible at source level: reproject_clouds produces
native normalized previous UV using previous projection/camera and cloud wind.
It deliberately handles neither current nor previous raster scale. Only d2's
previous c11/c12 address multiplication and active-rectangle footprint clamps
need the previous scale; native c14 depth and current consumers stay unchanged.

Concrete counterexamples: at normalized u=.8 a 1→.75 switch currently reads
prior c11/c12 at .6 instead of .8. A .75→1 switch reads .8 outside the prior .75
active rectangle. Both errors precede the reset branch repair; retaining old
history without changing these addresses is unsafe.

texture_min_4x4 at d2 lines 109–126 is four textureGather calls at ±2 native
texels, not a contiguous four-wide bounding footprint. Let b=floor(P-.5) for
P=coordinate*textureSize. The two axis pairs are b-2,b-1 and b+2,b+3, a six-wide
bounding footprint with gaps. Merely substituting previous scale leaves border
reads unsafe. Catmull-Rom fast at bicubic lines 129–167 uses center
floor(P-.5)+.5, outer centers -1/+2 and paired interior bilinear taps. Its
footprint must be checked against actual previous raster pixel centers, not
texture allocation size alone.

At native 2976×1672, .75 cloud-history edge is 2232×1254; .70 edge is
2083.2×1170.4. Quarter current-cloud allocation is 744×418; .75 edge is
558×313.5 and .70 edge is 520.8×292.6. Fractional raster boundaries require
explicit pixel-center/coverage and integer source-clamp proof. The source's
ivec2(size*scale-1) clamp and raster coverage must not be assumed identical.

Proposed additive transport: a separate versioned remapping extension with
previous actual-frame global enable and a certified pure-global-transition
flag, all from the existing immutable CoreUniformFrame snapshot. Keep temporal
v1 and historyReset semantics unchanged. Only same notifier/world, consecutive
valid snapshots, previous global 0/1, and exactly an enabled-only core change
may bypass cloud reset; preset/near/far/transition/debug changes, missing or
invalid transport, startup/reload/world/gaps/recovery remain hard resets. Shader
maps prior global to 1/.75; Java must not pretend to know arbitrary static shader
options. TAA can retain its conservative reset independently.

Assume private ON, TAA/TAAU, non-Voxy, Overworld, unchanged native framebuffer
and attachments, cloud divisor 4, valid consecutive actual rendering frames and
the same pipeline/options. Java transports previous global state, not a universal
previous shader scale: this adapter maps binary enable to 1/.75. Arbitrary static
fallback, resize/reallocation, missing cloud draws and option changes remain
uncertified. Root decides whether to implement the candidates described below.

## Complete cloud dependency inventory

Line numbers refer to R2 sources extracted under
`build/cloud-history-scale-remap-r1/source/shaders/`.

| Source | Required scale and interpretation |
| --- | --- |
| d2 vertex :20; fragment :186–195 | Current rectangle, current quarter fetch/clamp and current terrain depth keep current scale. Never substitute globally. |
| d2 :240–245,273–275 | Existing normalized uv cap .95 selects an approximate distance neighborhood. Previous c12 multiplication uses prior scale; each ±2 gather requires prior-footprint bounds. Current apparent distance remains in the minimum. |
| d2 :129–179,291 | World/cloud-wind reprojection produces normalized previous screen space. Projection explicitly suppresses jitter; no prior-scale or prior-jitter substitution needed here. |
| d2 :294–309 | Previous cloud coordinate clamp, c11 Catmull taps and c12 data sample require prior active extent and prior scale. |
| d2 :311–329 | c14 prior depth stays native normalized at fixed half-linear allocation. Preserve unclamped previous_uv for screen/terrain/hand/NaN/world-age rejection. |
| d2 :337–371 | Camera displacement/frame time/world distance are unchanged. Neighborhood clamping reads current quarter-cloud texels; existing unbounded ±1 current texelFetch border remains a separate boundary. |
| d2 :373–406 | Prior distance/age/ambient come from remapped c12. Checkerboard phase/modulo remain current destination-grid decisions, not rescaled old phases. |
| clouds/sampling.glsl :9–18 | Newly written c11/c12 age, distance, scattering/transmittance and lightning ambient keep current scale. Current mip/filter border safety is independent of prior remapping. |
| d4 fragment :153 | c11 mipmaps are enabled for current cloud consumption. Prior implicit texture() taps need a verified level-zero contract or explicit LOD to avoid stale mip borders. |

c11 RGB is scattering and alpha physical transmittance. c12 X is world apparent
distance, Y accumulated-frame age, Z indirect scattering for lightning. Resample
all channels at the same prior coordinate. Do not scale alpha, distance, ambient

# Photon temporal inputs and deterministic capture proposal

Source/bytecode audit checkpoint: 2026-10-04, Photon v1.3b and pinned Iris 1.8.12.
Research only while the main matrix is live. Only this document was written;
no shader/mod/profile edits, compilers or clients were run. The repeated premium

cannot identify which unmeasured state caused that difference.

## The cloud clock is world age, not frameTimeCounter

Photon `shaders.properties` defines:

```text
world_age = ((worldDay % 128) * 24000.0 + worldTime) / 20.0
```

Cloud coverage, volumetric Worley detail, altocumulus, congestus and cirrus wind
use this custom `world_age`. No cloud-density or weather include reads
`frameTimeCounter`; the cloud programs declare it but the density functions
consume world age. `WorldTimeUniforms` bytecode derives worldTime from client
level day time modulo 24000 and worldDay from the same value divided by 24000.
Current ComparisonClient applies `time set 1800` and `doDaylightCycle false` for
the storm, which should fix worldDay 0 and world_age 90 once acknowledged by the
client. That is a source-based expectation; exported day_time 1800 does not
currently record the actual Iris/custom uniform values.

With original resolved CLOUDS_SCALE 10 and default speeds:

| Layer | Shader-coordinate wind speed per world_age second | Equivalent world-block displacement |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Cumulus | 25 at 30 degrees | 2.5 blocks/second; x≈2.165, z=1.25 |
| Altocumulus | 25 at 60 degrees | 2.5 blocks/second; x=1.25, z≈2.165 |
| Congestus | 20 at 30 degrees | 2 blocks/second |
| Cirrus | 40 at 90 degrees | 4 blocks/second |

These are coordinate mappings, not measured live motion. With frozen day time,
world_age should not advance merely because the client runs longer. A changed
worldDay by one would change world_age by 1200 seconds and displace cumulus
coverage 3000 world blocks, despite equal time-of-day. Capture full day time and
actual worldDay/world_age to exclude it. Existing raw reports have full
`day_time=1800`, so they already make that day mismatch less plausible here.

Cumulus coverage uses `pos + cameraPosition.xz*10 + wind*world_age`; its noise
UV frequencies are 0.000002 and0.000027 divided by CLOUDS_CUMULUS_SIZE. Default
world-age-driven UV rates therefore have vector magnitudes0.00005 and0.000675
per world-age second. Bubbly/swirl detail sees the camera-shifted position plus
1.2/1.4 times wind respectively, at frequencies0.0009/0.005; default UV-speed
magnitudes are0.027 and0.175 per world-age second. Congestus coverage also adds
`50*squared(altitude_fraction)` to world_age locally; that is spatial shear,
not a wall-clock dependency. These paths can change actual density work if
world age differs, but freezing frameTimeCounter alone does not freeze them.

## Uncaptured state that can change cloud work

The most concrete additional input is **Iris wetness**, separate from the
Minecraft rain value exported by the harness. `CommonUniforms` registers
wetness as a SmoothedFloat driven by rainStrength, using pack wetness/dryness
half-life values. Pinned defaults are 600/200; `SmoothedFloat` multiplies each
by 0.1 before applying exponential decay. The effective default half-lives are
60 seconds when increasing and 20 seconds when decreasing. Photon declares no
override in its GLSL sources. The smoother initializes from its first observed
rainStrength and updates using Iris Timer.getLastFrameTime.

An idealized immediate rain step from 0 to 1 gives wetness about 0.333 after 35
seconds and 0.470 after 55; gradual Minecraft rain ramps change those values.
The current35-second warmup therefore does not prove wetness convergence.
A reused storm save may begin already raining on the next JVM, initializing
wetness differently from its initial copied forest save. That mechanism is
plausible, not demonstrated by the current reports: initial rain/wetness and
actual wetness during measurement were not captured. A fully wet steady state
would produce the same wetness across runs; do not assume every run starts dry.

Photon's `include/weather/core.glsl` adds wetness directly to humidity and
0.33 * wetness to wind before clamp01. Random weather temperature/humidity use
world_age at `0.37*golden_ratio/600` times their speed options; wind uses
`0.5*golden_ratio/600`. Daytime and smoothed biome values modify these fields.
`include/weather/clouds.glsl` converts them into layer coverage, stratus blend,
shape detail, altitude scale, extinction and congestus blend. RainStrength also
changes extinction/scattering and cirrus coverage directly. More density can
increase lighting samples or reach opacity termination earlier, so the sign of
its timing effect cannot be predicted simply as "more clouds means slower".

Additional fields to record rather than assume matched:

- Actual wetness and rainStrength, worldDay/worldTime/world_age and moonPhase.
- Smoothed biome_temperature/humidity/category weights and biome_may_rain/snow;
  the properties use smooth histories. Equal final camera position does not
  expose their initial state or prove identical convergence.
- world_age_changed and daylight_cycle_enabled, derived through smooth
  expressions; changes invalidate cloud temporal history or alter wind
  compensation in reprojection.
- Actual frameCounter, its phase at measurement start/end, frameTimeCounter,
  real frameTime and cloud history age. The cloud accumulation limit is 20 frames.
- Actual resolved cloud parameters or a CPU equivalent derived from captured
  uniform inputs, plus rain/thunder and last camera matrices. No GPU readback is
  needed merely to capture values before they are uploaded.

## Actual march/noise dependence

Cumulus maximum primary count is `uint(mix(40,20,abs(ray_dir.y)))` in the current
profile. ShaderLOD caps that count using the entry-distance tier. Lighting starts
at 6 steps and ambient at 2; Performance medium budgets are roughly half with
minimum lighting 2/ambient 1 and primary 4. Those caps do not describe executed
steps. The primary loop breaks when transmittance falls below 0.075; empty-density
samples skip secondary lighting/scattering. Later layers can be omitted when
combined transmittance falls below 1e-3. Cloud weather and density thus control
branch/loop work even with the same maximum settings.

`d1_clouds` computes spatial noise and applies `r1(frameCounter/checkerboard_area,
seed)`, where r1 is `fract(seed + n/phi1)` and checkerboard_area is upscale squared.
Premium upscale 1 advances that seed every rendered frame; default upscale 4
advances its outer sequence per 16 frames and cycles checkerboard offsets.
The same dither also chooses probabilistic distance tiers inside transition
bands. Secondary optical rays use hashes of jittered sample position.
Starting at a different frameCounter changes sampled density and tier choices.
Across enough frames this should average many phases, but equal wall durations
sample different counts and do not establish an identical phase sequence.

Do not freeze frameCounter for the performance proof: that would disable its
normal stochastic/temporal behavior and could create a special rendering
workload. Keep it advancing, log phase/count, and retain paired repetitions.

## Exact Iris seam for an optional static animation clock

The relevant class is `net.irisshaders.iris.uniforms.SystemTimeUniforms`, not
IrisTimeUniforms (the latter publishes calendar/currentDate/currentTime fields).
Its `addSystemTimeUniforms` binds PER_FRAME:

```text
frameCounter     <- SystemTimeUniforms.COUNTER (IntSupplier)
frameTime        <- TIMER.getLastFrameTime()
frameTimeCounter <- TIMER.getFrameTimeCounter()
```

`SystemTimeUniforms$Timer.beginFrame(long)` derives integer milliseconds from
elapsed nanoseconds, divides by1000 into seconds, updates lastFrameTime and adds
it to frameTimeCounter, wrapping at 3600 seconds. Its public getter is an exact
small seam for a future **devClient-only**, opt-in return-value mixin:
`getFrameTimeCounter()F`, remap false, cancellable HEAD or RETURN, require 1.
When a finite `shaderlod.dev.shaderClockSeconds` property is present, publish
that chosen constant; otherwise preserve the real getter. Do not mutate
beginFrame, lastFrameTime, real elapsed timing or counter state. Restrict behavior
to the development harness, exclude the mixin from the released mod and record
mode/value in fingerprints and measurement exports.

Apply the static value from in-world warmup onward, not at capture start, to
avoid a clock jump after histories have converged. Keep frameCounter and actual
frameTime advancing for TAA/checkerboard/noise and motion metrics. Freezing the
getter also does **not** freeze wetness: SmoothedFloat reads getLastFrameTime,
which deliberately remains real. This seam is useful for directly animated
water waves, aurora, air-fog noise and other frameTimeCounter consumers, but
cannot alone settle the cloud density question.

For the cloud static control, first record wetness. A separate future dev-only
wetness uniform-supplier override, before upload in CommonUniforms registration,
can publish a shared0 or 1 value for both original and ShaderLOD profiles. Keep
real rainStrength unchanged and clearly name the control as fixed shader
wetness; it selects an explicitly artificial steady shader weather state.
Do not override all SmoothedFloat getters, which would corrupt biome/eye/history
smoothers. Preserve the existing supplier and install a narrow wetness-only
registration wrapper when the optional property is absent. That seam needs
separate bytecode/application tests and logged actual supplied values.

## Conservative certificate

All equations are per RGB channel, for finite nonnegative inputs. Write
`r = rayleigh_scattering_coeff`, `m = mie_extinction_coeff`,
`s = mie_scattering_coeff`, `A = ambient_color`, `C = light_color`,
`k = max(skylight, eye_skylight)` for geometry (1 for sky),
`f = 1 - .9 rainStrength`, `I = 1/(4π)`, and

```
P(c) = Σ[i=0..3] .5^i × [.7 HG(c,.5×.7^i) + .3 HG(c,-.2×.7^i)]
qR = G × [2 A I k + C f × 1.875 I]
qM = G × (s/m) × [2 A I k + C f × P(c)]
Q = max(qR, qM)
```

Here `c` is the actual normalized ray/light cosine and `G ≤ 1.75` bounds the
original evening multiplier; clamp01 blindness/darkness only reduces light.
Taking G=1.75 is conservative. Four direct order weights sum to 1.875. The
original shadow result lies in [0,1] for supported ordinary depth behavior;
the colored branch clamps color into this interval too, but exclude that branch
from a first adapter pending its own sampler/domain qualification.

For one cell, `dτ = r dR + m dM`. Original visible integration is at most
`T_before (1-exp(-dτ))/dτ`; the eps denominator can only reduce it. Its maximum
colored source per optical depth is Q because a nonnegative weighted mixture of
Rayleigh and Mie source ratios cannot exceed their maximum. Summing cells
telescopes:

```
remaining scattering ≤ Q × T_current × (1 - T_remaining) ≤ Q × T_current
transmittance difference after stopping ≤ T_current
```

Therefore a tail may stop if **every channel** satisfies
`T_current ≤ εT` and `Q T_current ≤ εS`. Keep current partial accumulations and
T, then run the original final lighting block. No later unseen shadow edge can
violate this bound: it already assumes maximum illumination in every remaining
cell. Distance, apparent smoothness or preceding lit cells cannot substitute
for this certificate. Preserve all original visited cell locations/counts,
light/shadow integration, sky/water branches and distant lighting cues until
their remaining contribution is bounded.

`s/m` is not safely clamped to one: Photon sandstorm additions can have channel
ratios above one. If m=0 with s>0, any coefficient/palette is negative/nonfinite,
cosine/dither/rain/skylight is invalid, bridge/source is unknown, or inputs cannot
be certified, retain original work. Handle the genuinely zero numerator case
explicitly rather than dividing by zero. Flat coefficients/palette are constant
along this particular ray; this proof does not automatically transfer to a pack
with unbounded emissive/point-light samples along the ray.

Whole-ray omission is the same principle with T=1 and a conservative optical
depth envelope. For valid clipped geometry segment minimum height ymin, positive
falloff half-life Hj/start Zj, original dither in [0,1] and normalized noise in
[0,1], define

```
DRmax = .5 × fog_intensity × L × 2^min((ZR-ymin)/HR, 0)
DMmax = 2  × fog_intensity × L × 2^min((ZM-ymin)/HM, 0)
τmax = r DRmax + m DMmax
a = 1-exp(-τmax)
```

The neutral return `(scattering=0, transmittance=1)` has attenuation difference
≤a and scattering difference ≤Q a. Require `a≤εT` and `Q a≤εS`. The below-sea
fade only reduces density, so omitting it in the envelope is safe. This max-height
envelope bounds **Photon's actual discrete samples**. A continuous analytical
height integral alone does not: eight left samples of exp(-x) over [0,1] sum
.672451 versus continuous .632121, an underbound of 6.38%. Do not use that shortcut
to certify the original dithered grid.

These are floating-point-independent mathematical HDR bounds, not yet conservative
driver implementations. Outward rounding and safety margins, finite guards,
actual normalized sampler/texture behavior, RGBA16 transmittance quantization,
RGB16F scattering quantization, and consumer filtering must be qualified. For a
nonnegative background B, composition error is at most `B εT + εS`; the background
has no universal finite bound in this source interface. Exposure, tone mapping,
TAA and bloom do not turn chosen HDR budgets into a proved displayed tolerance.
Representative still/motion/shaft quality remains necessary.
